c1184.summary: A salutation to Shiva, whose very body is nada (musical sound), and from whose five faces the seven notes arose.
m: With mind and head bowed, I salute Shankara, whose body is nada, always —
the giver of joy, the essence of the Sama Veda, best of the Vedas — again and again;
who delights in the art of the seven notes sa ri ga ma pa dha ni, born of his five faces beginning with Sadyojata,
who vanquished Death, pure of heart, protector of Tyagaraja.

c2809.summary: Musical knowledge without devotion does not lead to the right path.
m: O mind, can knowledge of music without devotion lead to the right path?
(The music) worshipped by Bhringi, Nataraja, Hanuman, Agastya, Matanga, Narada and others —
one with devotion knows right from wrong, knows that the worlds are illusion,
and knows how to conquer the six inner enemies beginning with desire — so it is for Tyagaraja.

c2263.summary: Meditation on Rama is the true holy bath; ritual dips cannot wash away inner impurity.
m: Meditation is the true bath in the Ganga, O mind.
However often you dip in rainwater, will the inner stains of deceit and treachery wash away?
Shunning others' wealth and women, rising above slander and harm to others,
longing for Sri Rama who shines on earth — this is the Rama Tyagaraja came to know.

c1350.summary: Who can equal Rama — with a devoted wife and brothers whose every word is honey?
m: O Rama, who is your equal, uplifter of the Raghu race?
Your wife is like a tender shoot of the marjoram, a parrot in the cage of devotion;
and you have brothers whose every word drips honey —
O Hari, jewel of Tyagaraja's family, of gentle speech.

c2230.summary: Why wander in side lanes when the royal road of devotion to Rama is there?
m: When there's a fine royal highway, why wander in the lanes, O mind?
When rich milk and cream are at hand, why drink brackish water?
The form most beautiful to the eye, the name that shines on the lips of three-eyed Shiva, on which Tyagaraja meditates,
devotion to Sri Rama of Saketa, the God who dwells within — (that is the royal road).

c1700.summary: Tyagaraja asks Sita and Lakshmana to tell him the joy of standing beside Rama and serving him.
m: Won't you tell me well the joy of standing beside him and serving him?
O Sita, whose face outshines the moon, and Saumitri — on either side of Rama,
do you bow to him with your body? Do you sing his name with love?
Do you hold him in your mind and forget yourselves? Tell Tyagaraja kindly, you two.

c2561.summary: Lakshmana's fortune is the greatest fortune — he serves Rama closely and sees him in his true nature.
m: Lakshmana's fortune is fortune indeed — Saumitri's fortune is the true fortune;
seating the Lord of Sita on the wondrous jewelled bed of Shesha (and serving him) —
as Rama sang wonderful ragas in alapana, his body thrilled with joy;
praising and beholding the true essence of Sri Rama, praised by Tyagaraja — (that is) Saumitri's fortune.

c2930.summary: A scene of service: betel is offered to Rama while Lakshmana and Shatrughna attend on him.
m: Offer the betel roll — do not forsake me.
Thinking again and again of the fine betel rolls from the hand of the Earth's daughter,
Saumitri, honoured by kings, and his younger brother stand radiant holding the golden spittoon, O God of gods;
nutmeg, cardamom, mace, areca nut and betel leaves — Tyagaraja offers them with love, O best of kings.

c1291.summary: There is no liberation for those without realisation, devotion and knowledge of music; nada is the path.
m: Is there liberation on earth for those who are not liberated while living,
for those without direct realisation, true devotion to you, and knowledge of music?
From the union of breath and inner fire, the pranava nada arises and becomes the seven svaras —
they do not know the mind of Shiva who delights in playing the veena, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c1053.summary: Chant Rama's name knowing its meaning: words like Rama, Arka and Aja have lowly and exalted meanings, and only the right understanding helps.
m: Knowing its meaning, chant the name with thought of Rama, O mind —
stilling all thoughts, even for a moment, (knowing) the true nature of the saving form.
'Rama' is also a word for fickle-eyed women — for those who think so, the fight with desire goes on;
'Rama' is the name of the Brahman of the Ramayana — knowing that, the sorrows of birth end.
'Arka' is a name for the milkweed plant — how will monkey minds (that think so) be cured?
'Arka' is a name for the Sun — knowing that, the darkness of false reasoning ends.
'Aja' is a word for a goat — (thinking so,) how will true longing be fulfilled?
'Aja' is a name for Brahma, lord of speech — victory comes (from knowing) the one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2380.summary: Will the elders' saying — that God is truly there for those who truly seek — be proven today?
m: 'For those who truly seek, he is truly there' — will the elders' words be proven today?
Why don't you come to us, who long to see your lovely face with mirror-bright cheeks?
Giving up sleep, lovingly holding the tambura, with a pure mind and true pitch,
those who worship you without fail — you are the compassionate one who protects such devotees, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2251.summary: Tyagaraja wonders how he could ever repay his debt to Rama, who made his songs known far and wide.
m: O son of Dasharatha, can I ever repay my debt to you, O one of most holy name?
O crown of connoisseurs, who made (my songs) shine in far-off lands to my heart's content!
Seeing that, in the Kali age, even the best of poets without devotion cannot grasp the true feeling,
you taught through kirtanas that worldly and spiritual fulfilment both come (through devotion) — you who are worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c2286.summary: Where is Rama hiding? He came for Prahlada and Sugriva — why not now for his devotee?
m: Where is he hiding? Will he take pity and come here today, O mind?
Why this fickleness? Hear my plea — (he who used) to nurture devotees as before —
once, when Hiranyakashipu in hatred inflicted every torment on his own son,
was he not inside the pillar for steadfast Prahlada, who could not bear it? How, then, (not) now?
Earlier, when Indra's son (Vali) in pride beat Sugriva, son of the Sun — unable to bear the sight,
did he not stand behind the palmyra tree to lovingly protect him? How, then, (not) now?
To destroy the evil deeds of past births and to seize and crush the six inner enemies,
and moreover to protect steadfast true devotees in this world, and Tyagaraja — (where is he hiding?)

c2741.summary: A description of Lord Ranganatha of Srirangam setting out in a royal procession.
m: The King goes in procession — come and see, Kasturi Ranga!
Mounted on a horse, with all kings serving him, wearing radiant ornaments of the nine gems — Ranga!
In holy Srirangam on the banks of the Kaveri, coming in splendour along the Chitra street,
as the gods worship him with flowers and Tyagaraja sings, imagining it — Ranga in all his glory.

c1467.summary: When ten million holy rivers are present at Dhanushkoti (Rama's feet), why wander to pilgrimages?
m: When ten million rivers are in Dhanushkoti, why do you wander, O mind?
For the great ones who directly behold the dark, handsome form again and again —
the Ganga was born from his anklet; the Kaveri shines beside Ranganatha;
overflowing with love, Tyagaraja praises Sri Raghunatha — hear his plea.

c2283.summary: What use are wealth, rituals, fame or learning without Rama's grace?
m: What does it matter what one does, if one lacks the grace of Lord Sri Rama,
among those who, slaves to desire and delusion, do not know the ways of Sri Rama?
What if one has comforts? What if one adorns one's wife with jewels? What if
one knows the play of Manmatha's bow? — among those without the grace of the lotus-eyed one.
What if one performs sacrifices? What if, with wealth, one celebrates the birth of sons? What if one takes
on another's child as one's own? — among those without the grace of auspicious Sri Rama.
What if one builds mansions? What if many there marry? What if one knows how to
please women? — among those without the grace of peerless Rama.
What if one rules a kingdom? What if one is revered among many? What if, with streams of ghee,
one feeds rice (to many)? — among those without the grace of revered Rama.
What if one becomes a guru? What if one looks weighty to the eye? What if
one teaches great mantras to others? — among those without the grace of the Lord praised by Tyagaraja.

c1514.summary: Only what is destined comes to pass; Tyagaraja recalls how the great devotees were blessed.
m: Only if it is destined will it come to pass, O granter of wishes.
Not understanding the ways of the Kali age, I blamed you; it comes only if good fortune is written on my head.
The foremost devotees — Narada, Prahlada, Parashara and Ramadasa —
the way they worshipped Sri Raghurama's feet so well — (if it is destined) for Tyagaraja now, (it will come).

c1426.summary: Tyagaraja greets Rama, who has walked all the way to protect him, and describes his form.
m: Have you walked all the way here to protect me, O lord of my life?
O lotus-eyed one, knowing the secret of my heart — that seeing your face is my very life —
with a body like the sapphire of Indra, with strings of pearls on your chest,
with the gleam of the arrow and Kodanda bow in your hand, with the Earth's daughter — O one worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c1128.summary: Tyagaraja asks the enchanting Rama to speak sweetly to him, and describes how gods took animal forms to serve him.
m: Enchanting Rama, whose face outshines the moon, speak to me sweetly.
Enchanting Rama, first among gods, my love for you has blossomed.
Hearing of the glory of your incarnation as a man on earth, the gods, kinnaras, kimpurushas, vidyadharas, Indra, Brahma,
the sun, the moon and others melted, and with love, in the forms of beasts, birds and monkeys, on the mountain
they long served you, O shining Lord of Sita, forgetting themselves — O giver of boons to Tyagaraja, Lord of the whole world.

c2328.summary: Who is our refuge except Rama? Tyagaraja pleads against Rama's delay and coolness.
m: Who is there, other than you, as our refuge?
Protector of the sacrifice, ever festive, Lord of Sita!
Won't your grace come upon me? Won't you listen? Aren't you the enemy of Mura? Won't you speak kindly?
Is this proper toward me? Is it a quarrel? Is there any difference between us?
Is it right to tease me by not coming? Is it indifference, or am I loathsome to you, Rama?
O moon-faced one, I have longed for you — enough now, O one of holy fame, for us.
Lord of Lakshmi, enemy of demons, you went away without knowing your servant; O one worshipped by Shiva,
protector of all, my light, self-luminous one, for us —
O king, why this stiffness? Worshipped by Tyagaraja — I cannot bear this delay, O king;
do you hesitate to protect me, O king, our wish-fulfilling tree?

c1301.summary: A tender song inviting Rama to rest in the devotee's heart and recover from all his labours for his devotees.
m: O one praised by Shiva, rest in my heart, so your weariness may pass.
Saviour from worldly bondage — so the weariness of talking at length with me may pass, O lotus-(eyed one),
dear to Hanuman — so the weariness of wandering for his sake may pass,
so the weariness of coming to my house and testing me may pass, O lotus-(eyed one),
so the weariness of my not offering you fine food may pass,
so the weariness of acting as though it didn't matter may pass, O lotus-(eyed one),
so the weariness of resolving to protect me mightily may pass,
you are Tyagaraja's lord — so your weariness may pass, O lotus-(eyed one).

c2441.summary: Tyagaraja asks why Rama's compassion has not come to him, when he has no other protector.
m: Won't your compassion come to me?
Who is there to say otherwise, O Kalyana Rama?
Long ago I knew there was none else to protect me — O scion of the Solar race, why such delay?
If I praise you as master of all and you forgive me, would that lessen your greatness?
Rama, Rama, Rama, dweller in Tyagaraja's heart — is it fair that my mind is in turmoil? Come quickly.
